newsitem.title: UK: Options - LME December declaration runs smoothly.
newsitem.headline: Options - LME December declaration runs smoothly.

text.p: Declarations against London Metal Exchange (LME) December copper traded options passed by smoothly on Wednesday and there were few surprising developments.
Traders said the December date remained close to the $2,300 level through a generally slow LME pre-market, and this was the strike that was the focus of attention.

Open interest at this strike was not over-large, while overall option hedging was concluded well in advance. "As things went, it passed by smoothly...I would say that there was probably 50 percent declared at $2,300," one said.
"Not all the $2,300 puts were declared...some of the calls were declared. The market-makers were left, on balance, a little short of copper after declaration," another trader said.
Momentary concern was caused by a brief power failure at the London Clearing House (LCH) around 1000 gmt, but the declaration process was extended by 10 minutes to accomodate this.
"It was a bit of a damp squib, really. A lot of the $2,300s were not declared, aluminium $1,500 calls were declared and that was it," one said.

In the run-up to Wednesday's options, copper has been the centre of market attention, and a week ago it had appeared that the upside call strikes at $2,500 and $2,600 in particular, where there was large open interest, would be in the frame.
But over the last two days, lower LME prices and narrowing spreads meant these options, barring something completely unexpected, were not going to be exercised.
Call option open interest at $2,600 was a whopping 6,807 lots, but at $2,300 it was a much more manageable 880 contracts. Put options open at $2,300 totalled 1,465 lots.
Just after declaration prices eased by perhaps $3, but there was no obvious follow-through reaction.
"Down at these levels, I don't think anybody was particularly short of options," a trader said.

The action on the underlying futures market reflected the low-key nature of the declarations, with LME three months prices trading aimlessly between $2,195 and $2,200. Recent trade was at $2,195, up $12 from overnight.
In aluminium there were around 636 lots of $1,500 calls in the money and declared, while around 590 lots of puts were not exercised.
